mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, higher discount rates reduce the present value of expected corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified FEDFUNDS rise (p > 0.05) or FEDFUNDS rise < 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment growth) of at least 50,000 jobs is associated with stronger consumer demand and corporate optimism, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥50,000 in the following month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite PAYEMS increase ≥50,000 (p < 0.05) or no significant effect detected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of over 2% in the prior month reduces economic momentum, resulting in negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
regime_hint: Economic contraction or weak growth phase
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during INDPRO declines >2% or INDPRO declines are absent.

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (housing starts) rises by more than 10% in the next quarter, it signals renewed construction activity and consumer confidence, driving positive S&P 500 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >10% over the next 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive during the HOUST surge (p > 0.05) or HOUST increase ≤10%.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in UNRATE (unemployment) below 3.8% for two consecutive months indicate a tightening labor market, which raises expected equity valuations and produces positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls for two consecutive months below 3.8%
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during the two consecutive UNRATE declines below 3.8% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in RSAFS (retail sales) of over 5% in the following month suggests consumer weakness, which predicts negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by >5% in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative during the RSAFS drop (p > 0.05) or RSAFS decline ≤5%.

mechanism_narrative: When both INDPRO and GDPC1 show simultaneous declines of at least 3% and 10% respectively over the next quarter, it signals dual supply shocks that depress market valuations and drive negative 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: both INDPRO ↓3% and GDPC1 ↓10% over the next 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during the simultaneous declines (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent CPIAUCSL inflation above 4%, the S&P 500 5-day forward return is expected to be negative as investors anticipate rate hikes that compress growth prospects.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative when CPIAUCSL >4% (p > 0.05) or inflation remains ≤4%.
